subject: general
question: Which of the following pair of dances belongs to Kerala?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali and Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam** pair of dances **belongs to Kerala**.
 
• Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are classical dance forms originating from Kerala, India.
 
• **Kathakali **is renowned for its **theatrical elements,** including elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, expressive face masks, and ornate ornaments.
 
• **Mohiniyattam **is characterized by its graceful movements, predominantly performed by women.
 
• It is often described as a blend of **Kathakali and Bharatanatyam styles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kathakali **remains popular in India, preserving its traditional practices. With over 500 Attakatha plays, many dating back to before the 20th century, Kathakali has a rich repertoire.
 
• Recent productions have expanded its horizons by incorporating stories from various cultures and mythologies, including those of Miguel de Cervantes, Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, and William Shakespeare.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is celebrated for its elegance, typically performed as solo recitals by female dancers.
 
• The name "Mohiniyattam" derives from "Mohini," the feminine aspect of Lord Vishnu, signifying the "dance of Mohini."
 
• The dance narrates the tale of Mohini, an enchantress avatar of the divine in Vaishnavism.
